parsed.reason: The acknowledgment is brief and avoids invention, which is good. However, "Got it - Nora is 3." is a pure database-row recitation of the single fact the parent gave. It adds nothing beyond mirroring the input verbatim, which reads mechanical rather than warm or plain-spoken. A slightly more natural phrasing (e.g. "Thanks — we've got Nora (3) noted.") would feel like a competent human wrote it without padding or hype. It doesn't cross into bad territory (no exclamation marks, no invented facts, no corporate voice), but the flat echo of the parent's own words keeps it from feeling like a genuine acknowledgment.
